source.title: Empirical Analysis of the Hessian of Over-Parametrized Neural Networks
source.authors: Levent Sagun; Utku Evci; V. Güney; Y. Dauphin; L. Bottou

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares large- and small-batch training and reports test performance, but uses a sequential batch-size switch rather than the fixed-epoch comparison in V5.
record.gate_note: The Hessian spectrum and eigenvalue results do not themselves measure the generalization gap named in V7. Results cited from prior work, including Zhang et al. and Keskar et al., are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study reports held-out accuracy after sequential large-batch then small-batch training, but does not compare batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget as V5 specifies. Its Hessian and basin-connectivity results do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that Hessian degeneracy makes isolated-basin descriptions misleading and demonstrate a large-batch solution and its small-batch continuation connected without a loss barrier despite different generalization performance. They interpret this as evidence that the observed gap need not arise from reaching different basins.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes batch size sequentially on one trained AlexNet and evaluates test accuracy and interpolation; V5 describes comparisons under fixed epoch budgets across classifiers and language models.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracy differs between the batch-size phases; batch size changes from 1,000 to 32 during continued training.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, bare AlexNet gains approximately 1% test accuracy after switching from batch size 1,000 to 32 and training for another 25,000 updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued small-batch training from a large-batch endpoint can improve held-out accuracy; this sequential experiment does not isolate the batch-size effect.

fits_no_version.finding: The large-batch endpoint and its small-batch continuation have different test accuracies but no loss barrier along their straight-line interpolation; separate MNIST experiments find larger positive Hessian eigenvalues with large batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different generalization performance can occur within a connected low-loss region, and batch size can affect Hessian curvature. These measures do not test magnitude-aware sharpness as defined in V7.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (workshop track)
record.problems: The batch-size comparison is sequential on one model, not an independent fixed-epoch comparison. The approximately 1% accuracy change has no uncertainty estimate, and the figure does not provide exact phase values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No other results directly measure a V5 held-out performance outcome. The Hessian spectrum comparisons in Figures 1–6 measure eigenvalues, not the batch-size generalization penalty; cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: Own experiments comparing random-label memorization with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; the width sweep reports Hessian spectra.
Held-out performance comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer generalization and its dependence on tuning.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under matched epoch budgets, and whether adapted recipes remove a penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Neither the unmatched training budgets nor the approximately 1% improvement warrants a limits_scope verdict on V5. Additional Hessian and interpolation results were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper cites Zhang et al. but does not itself test fitting random labels or generalization on natural labels.
Network-size sweeps measure Hessian eigenvalues, not test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected generalization comparison is reported.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is reported.

The CIFAR-10 experiment changes batch size sequentially from 1,000 to 32, at a fixed number of iterations per phase; it does not compare independently trained models under a fixed epoch budget or test recipe adaptations.
The paper compares Hessian eigenvalues across batch-size settings but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test whether it ranks generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.

rows.subject: a bare AlexNet
rows.stage_stated: trained on the full CIFAR10 data
rows.operation_detail: Trained first with batch-size 1,000, then continued from that endpoint with batch-size 32; other settings, including constant learning rate, were kept the same.
rows.value: Part II reaches slightly better accuracy (about ∼ 1%).
rows.note: Sequential phase comparison; the paper describes an approximately 1% accuracy improvement toward the end of Part II, rather than reporting a numeric accuracy for each phase.
rows.check: The approximately 1% accuracy improvement is correctly reported, but follows 25,000 additional small-batch updates from the large-batch endpoint. Batch size and continued training are confounded, with no matched-epoch comparison or continued-large-batch control. This cannot establish V5's effect; 'partial' incorrectly treats a design mismatch as an incomplete effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR10 bare AlexNet, sequential switch from batch-size 1,000 to 32
reader_labels.reason: Part II is reported to improve accuracy by about ∼ 1%, but the sequential, fixed-iteration setup does not establish the fixed-epoch large-batch penalty; see R1.
